About This Job
We are looking for a candidate ready to leverage their Global regulatory experience in a dynamic, fintech environment. This is an exciting, hands-on opportunity working directly with our world-class Marketing organisation to launch compliant financial promotions.
Your mission:
Wise has already pioneered new ways for people to transfer money across borders and currencies. Our customers can also manage their hard-earned money with the World’s first platform to offer true international multi-currency accounts. Your mission is to enable our global marketing and product teams to launch new campaigns and manage our risk profile through a deep understanding of the regulatory requirements and Regulator’s expectations around them.
Here’s how you’ll be contributing to the Global Product Compliance & Risk team, in the first line:
Collaborate on Marketing Campaigns:
•
Empower Marketing & Product Teams to launch risk based, brand forward promotional campaigns across all channels;
•
Collaborate to design and implement a practical and comprehensive financial promotions framework;
•
Perform pre-launch and ongoing marketing compliance legal and regulatory analysis and risk assessments; and
•
Design scalable and customer-centric solutions to regulatory requirements;
•
Offer effective advice to Marketing and Product Managers on existing and forthcoming Regulations, gaps, and risks.
Manage and Mitigate Regulatory Risks and the Control Environment:
•
As part of the Global Regulatory Product Compliance Team, you will identify and manage Regulatory Risks across all financial promotions offered to and for customers globally;
•
Oversee the global control environment, designing effective, creative and targeted controls and evaluating the residual risk exposure;
•
Collaborate with Compliance colleagues, to ensure Wise Product Teams are constantly aware of the most recent regulations and guidance; and
•
Work with Marketing & Product Teams and the wider Risk & Compliance Team to implement and maintain Management Information that enables Wise to make informed decisions at the regional and Global levels.
Audit, issue management and remediation:
•
Conduct audit management and, where required, challenge audit findings in collaboration with Compliance second line and Product teams;
•
Develop and deliver effective issue management to mitigate regulatory risks;
This role will give you the opportunity to:
•
Grow your hands-on Fintech knowledge at full speed;
•
Keep compliance right at the heart of the marketing lifecycle, in a fast-moving environment;
•
Be empowered to identify ‘regulatory problems’ and take a lead in the solution design and implementation;
About you:
•
You have previous experience of approving financial promotions/advertising gained either as part of a Compliance or Marketing role
•
You have Financial Regulation advisory experience and are comfortable interpreting regulations (e.g. ASA requirements, COBS, UDAAP);
•
Ability to analyze and interpret complex regulatory frameworks and apply them effectively;
•
Ability to effectively communicate with Marketing Managers and Compliance and provide practical, actionable, and value added recommendations;
•
Problem solving attitude, with the ability to use regulations together with data to drive business decisions;
•
Experience (or interest) in working in a fast-growing environment and working directly with product teams;
•
Willing to travel, as Wise offices are located across different countries; and
•
Legally authorized to work in the UK
Some extra skills that would be great:
•
Experience working with marketing or product governance frameworks
•
Experience with Confluence, Jira, Risk and Controls software
•
Experience working with global teams

Additional Information
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/cliffordchance/.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The role
We advise many of the world's leading companies on public and private M&A, disposals, demergers, joint ventures, restructurings and high value commercial contracts with a particular focus on complex, cross-border transactions.
Our team works closely with antitrust specialists on merger control matters and collaborates with experts across finance, capital markets, litigation, tax, pensions, employment and real estate to deliver integrated advice.
We combine international deal execution skills with deep local market knowledge and sector-focused expertise. Our practice also covers corporate governance, regulatory compliance, intellectual property and technology advisory, providing clients with comprehensive support across all aspects of corporate activity.
Who you will work with
Our clients include many of the world's leading public and private corporations, investment banks and financial institutions, governments and international bodies.
Our unique service offering to clients is our top tier strength across M&A, private equity, antitrust, IP and funds alongside the deep corporate client base, combined with unrivalled strength and depth of expertise across practice areas and around our network.
We advise our clients on strategic corporate and M&A work, both domestic and international, with a particular focus on large, complex, cross-border transactions. Our work spans Europe, the US, the Middle East and APAC.
You will be working with a broad range of clients and the firm's other teams and practice areas, not only in London, but across the globe.
What you will be responsible for
As an Associate in our team, you will be working on some of the world's largest and most complex M&A transactions. Our lawyers provide a seamless integrated service across our network of offices and across different areas of expertise including public takeovers, private M&A, joint ventures, restructurings, secondary issues and advisory work.
You will provide legal and commercial expertise on complex M&A transactions, large-scale re-organisations and joint venture arrangements as well as corporate advisory work; across a wide range of sectors including financial services, energy and resources, consumer goods and retail, healthcare, industrials, real estate, aviation and technology.
You will be working as part of cross-border and interdisciplinary teams to advise on corporate finance activities, ensuring compliance with local laws and business requirements.
You will develop relationships with clients and actively engage in business development and thought leadership initiatives and seeking out opportunities for new work.
You will be drafting legal documents clearly and concisely, creating solutions using legal knowledge and commercial judgement to advise and support leading multi-national corporates.

Qualifications
Your experience
You will have a solid background in corporate work, gained at a city firm, or at an overseas common law practice with a highly regarded profile.   We are looking for proactive Associates who are able to think outside the box to create bespoke solutions for our clients' objectives.
You will:
•  have experience of advising on complex, multi-jurisdictional transactions.
• have an outstanding academic history and proven first rate legal skills, combined with a strong reputation amongst existing clients for providing commercial solutions, excellent transactional and management skills, and be recognised as a lawyer that is sought out by existing clients.
• be able to demonstrate excellent document drafting skills, strong communication and analytical skills along with a high level of commercial awareness.
• need to demonstrate that you can thrive in a team with high professional standards and a client-focused commercial approach. You will have had strong exposure of collaborating with multi-jurisdictional and multi-disciplinary teams.
It is also crucial that you can demonstrate an appetite for business development, client relationship management and thought leadership.

Additional Information
How we will support you
From your first day with us, you will have varied opportunities to continuously grow and development your skills and knowledge. From formal training, informal coaching and mentoring through to skills-based and technical training and on the job learning.
Hybrid working
This role follows our 'balanced' hybrid working approach and as long as business needs allow, you will be supported to work in a hybrid way in line with the hybrid working policy.
What we offer including our broad range of benefits and working environment
When you join Clifford Chance, you will have access to a broad range of benefits to support you across many aspects of your personal and professional life including financial, wellbeing, lifestyle, and family friendly benefits. For more information on what we offer specifically in the UK, please visit our What We Offer page on our career site.
Equal opportunities
At Clifford Chance, we understand that our true asset is our people. Inclusion is good for our team and their families, our firm and society.
We are committed to treating all employees and applicants fairly and equally regardless of their gender, gender identity and expression, marital or civil partnership status, race, colour, national or ethnic origin, social or economic background, disability, religious belief, sexual orientation, or age.  This applies to recruitment and selection, terms and conditions of employment including pay, promotion, training, transfer and every other aspect of employment.
We have a variety of flourishing employee networks. These networks are a place for colleagues to share experiences and advocate for change wherever they see an opportunity for improvement.
Our goal is to deliver an equality of opportunity, an equality of aspiration and an equality of experience to everyone who works in our firm.
Find out more about our inclusive culture here.

Business Operations Manager
Portsmouth – with Nationwide Travel
Permanent, full-time

The successful candidate will act as the Managing Director's operational lead, taking ownership of key business improvement projects, ensuring company-wide initiatives are delivered effectively, and providing the management information required to support informed decision-making. Business Improvement & Continuous Improvement
• Lead and deliver company-wide continuous improvement initiatives.
• Identify opportunities to improve business efficiency, productivity and service delivery.
• Develop and implement new business processes and procedures.
• Drive efficiency and cost-saving initiatives across the organisation.
• Monitor improvement plans and ensure agreed actions are successfully delivered.
• Track internal and external audit findings and ensure corrective actions are implemented.
Operational Excellence
• Standardise operational processes and record keeping across all business locations.
• Reduce duplication of activities, documentation and administrative tasks.
• Improve communication and collaboration between departments.
• Review existing ways of working and recommend practical improvements.
• Promote best practice and consistency throughout the business.
Business Management Systems
• Lead the implementation of new business system
• Support system optimisation to maximise business benefits.
• Improve data quality, integrity and reporting capability.
• Drive the digitalisation of paper-based processes.
• Coordinate system testing, user training and business-wide rollouts.
• Support users following implementation to maximise adoption.
Business Performance & Reporting
• Own the production of monthly business KPI reporting.
• Manage group company reporting requirements and ensure timely submission.
• Produce meaningful management information to support business performance and decision making.
• Track actions arising from leadership meetings and ensure completion.
Resource Planning & Business Support
• Maintain oversight of staff utilisation and operational capacity.
• Identify opportunities to improve resource allocation across locations.
• Support cross-site collaboration and sharing of resources.
• Work closely with department managers to improve operational planning.
• Provide operational support to the Managing Director on key strategic initiatives.
Leadership & Stakeholder Management
• Work collaboratively with senior managers across all departments.
• Build positive relationships across the wider business.
• Influence and support managers in implementing change.
• Communicate business improvements clearly and effectively.

Qualifications
• Working within a marine or MOD customer base, or working within the Industrial Cleaning/Engineering environment is essential.
• Proven experience in business operations
• Experience leading cross-functional improvement projects.
• Strong analytical and reporting skills with the ability to interpret business data
• Experience producing management information and KPI reporting.
• Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
• Excellent organisational and planning skills.

About This Job
Logistic Supply Specialist
Full-time
Logistic Specialists (Supply) are the Army’s Supply Chain Managers. Ammunition, weapons, materiel – the Army needs all kinds of supplies, all the time. Working in a warehouse, or in a field supply area that you have set up, you will be using state of the art software to demand, receive, issue, store and account for the Army’s equipment. You will also learn how to drive HGV’s and forklifts.
You can be employed in other organisations and undertake work placements with industries to understand best practice. You will also gain an understanding of IT systems used by other military alliances.
Find where you belong.
WORLD-CLASS TRAINING
You'll start with your initial military training which will teach you how to be a soldier - this will cover everything from fieldcraft to handling a rifle. If you join as a Junior Soldier (under 17 years 5 months), you’ll do a 23-week basic military training course at Harrogate. If you join as a Regular Soldier (over 17 years 1 month), you’ll do the regular 14-week adult basic training.
Next, you will undertake your 18-week Combat Logistician course at the Defence School of Transport in Leconfield. During this, you will earn your Category C+E Driving Licence and study general service driver modules. This training also gives you the opportunity to gain a broader knowledge on the Royal Logistic Corps functions and roles.
You will then complete your trade training at the Defence School of Logistics in Worthy Down to be qualified as a Logistic Supply Specialist Class 3. At this stage, you will be enrolled onto the Level 2 Warehouse Operative Apprenticeship. After 12 months in your Unit, you will complete the Class 2 upgrade assessment. Following a further two years, you will be eligible to complete the Class 1 course if successfully promoted to Lance Corporal.
GAIN QUALIFICATIONS
• Level 2 Certificate Logistics & Transport
• Level 2 Warehouse Operative Apprenticeship
SHOW PEOPLE WHAT YOU’RE CAPABLE OF
We'll be with you every step of the way as you move up the ranks. From the moment you begin your training you'll get all the support and encouragement you need to make a success of your career. Work hard and you'll soon get promoted, which means more responsibility and extra pay.
Become a Logistic Supply Specialist and you’ll:
-           Earn a starting salary of around £16,800 during Basic Training which will rise to around £21,400 after completing 26 weeks’ training or after completing your Initial Trade Training, if less than 26 weeks
-           Receive subsidised accommodation and facilities, increasing your disposable income
-           Receive free medical and dental health cover
-           Have the continuous access promotional opportunity and to continually progress your career
-           Be sponsored to earn valuable civilian-recognised qualifications
-           Take part in Adventurous Training and be able to play your favourite sports.
BELONG TO SOMETHING THAT MATTERS.
You should be:
• Regular Army age: 16.6 – 35.11 years
Fitness requirements:
• Mid-Thigh Pull 50kg
• Medicine Ball Throw 2.7m
• 2km run 11m 30s (11m for Junior Entry)
Our next deadline for application is 31st March 2023, with further opportunities ongoing throughout the year.
FIND WHERE YOU BELONG.

About This Job
The Portfolio Lead is accountable for delivery performance across a sub-domain of 4-6 pods (Engineering, Quality, Product). They lead the flow of value from idea to production, ensuring pods deliver with pace, predictability and understanding to outcomes.
They combine hands-on delivery leadership with AI-augmented ways of working and data-driven decision-making. They do not prescribe a single framework - instead they adapt approaches that best serve each pod's context.
They partner with Engineering and Product leadership to reduce waste, improve throughput and help pods achieve Autonomy, Accountability and Agreement to value outcomes.
What you will do
Pod Performance & Accountability
You are responsible for pod delivery performance across the sub-domain.
You will lead and communicate delivery health, risks and performance to leadership
Ensure pods operate as, self-organising units delivering value outcomes
Support pod leads with coaching, facilitation and conflict resolution
Ensure cross-pod agreement on priorities, dependencies and shared goals
Facilitate communication and collaboration between pods to promote knowledge sharing
Problem Solving
You will be an expert; deploy root cause analysis, systems thinking and structured techniques to analyse and guide out resolutions.
Be an escalation point for cross-pod blockers and systemic impediments
Identify patterns across pods that indicate deeper organisational or process issues
AI-Augmented Delivery
Champion AI agent adoption across pods - including coding agents, test generation, story creation, board health and deployment automation
Identify opportunities where AI can reduce toil, accelerate delivery or improve decision-making
Apply AI to improve delivery effectiveness, including workflow insights, risk prediction, and automation of reporting
Track and demonstrate the impact of AI on delivery performance
Flow & Efficiency
Monitor and improve delivery flow (lead time, cycle time, WIP, throughput) using Kanban and lean principles
Ensure WIP limits are respected and surface ageing items through Board Walks
Identify bottlenecks, ageing work and sources of delay across pods.
Improve through regular assessment and experimentation.
Support teams in breaking down work into deliverable, value-driven increments
Agile Ways of Working
Support and evolve the agile operating model for a pod-based environment focused on pace, not ceremony.
Adapt delivery approaches (Kanban, flow-based, lean) appropriate to each pod's needs
Ensure consistency of practice across pods without being prescriptive
Promote outcome-driven delivery vs output-driven activity
Guide teams to operate with autonomy and accountability
Metrics & Reporting
Define and maintain delivery metrics: cycle time, flow efficiency, lead time of initiative, PDLC compression, dependency reduction, rework rate, team satisfaction, and AI effectiveness
Build dashboards (cumulative flow diagrams, throughput charts, WIP ageing) that provide leadership visibility and lead informed decision-making
Analyse performance data to identify trends, patterns and areas for improvement
Use data to facilitate conversations and coach pods — not just track output
Stakeholder Management
Partner with Engineering and Product leadership at sub-domain level
Represent delivery health and risks in leadership forums
Build trusted relationships that allow fast decision-making

About This Job
We’re looking for talented and motivated students to join our Traffic Engineering team on an Industrial Placement, where you’ll gain hands-on experience, contribute to real projects, and develop technical skills that will kick-start your career.
As part of AECOM’s Transportation business line, you’ll work alongside experienced traffic engineers, transport planners, and technical specialists to help develop solutions that improve the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of transport networks.
Our work covers a wide range of traffic engineering projects, from junction and network assessments to traffic modelling, signal design, road safety, and the development of sustainable transport solutions. You’ll have the opportunity to work on projects for local authorities, National Highways, developers, and other public and private sector clients.
What you’ll do
Your placement will provide exposure to a variety of traffic engineering activities, which may include:
• Supporting the design and assessment of junctions, roundabouts, traffic signals, and urban road networks.
• Assisting with traffic modelling, microsimulation, and network analysis using industry-standard software such as Junctions, LinSig, and VISSIM.
• Supporting traffic impact assessments, transport assessments, feasibility studies, and scheme appraisals.
• Collecting, analysing, and interpreting traffic flow, speed, journey time, and other transport data to inform engineering decisions.
• Assisting with the development and assessment of traffic management and network improvement schemes.
• Supporting the preparation and assessment of traffic signal layouts and junction improvement proposals.
• Contributing to road safety assessments and audits, helping to identify potential issues and develop appropriate solutions.
• Supporting the development of active travel and sustainable transport schemes, considering the interaction between pedestrians, cyclists, public transport, and general traffic.
• Assisting with the preparation of technical reports, drawings, calculations, presentations, and other project documentation.
• Developing an understanding of relevant traffic engineering standards, guidance, legislation, and industry best practice.
• Attending site visits and traffic surveys to understand existing conditions and collect information to support project development.
• Working collaboratively with traffic engineers, highway engineers, transport planners, technicians, and other disciplines to deliver high-quality solutions for clients.
• Contributing to project meetings and developing an understanding of how technical recommendations are communicated to clients and stakeholders.

Qualifications
We’re looking for students who can demonstrate the following:
• Currently studying towards a degree in Civil Engineering, Transportation/Traffic Engineering, Highway Engineering, or a related discipline.
• Genuine interest in traffic engineering, transport planning, and the development of safe, efficient, and sustainable transport networks.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret and evaluate technical information and data.
• An interest in traffic modelling, junction design, network analysis, and transport data analysis.
• Good understanding of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
• Strong attention to detail, with good research, technical writing, and report-writing skills.
• Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical information clearly.
• Ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team, while demonstrating initiative when working independently.
• A self-motivated and enthusiastic approach, with a willingness to learn new software, tools, and technical methodologies.
• Commitment to continuous learning and professional development throughout the placement.
• A practical, adaptable, and solutions-focused approach to technical challenges.

• Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected for an advanced offer start.

About This Job
We are seeking an experienced and entrepreneurial Senior Business Development Manager to join our Wise Platform team. In this role, you will take full commercial ownership of driving our growth with financial institutions and banks across Switzerland.
You will help deliver world-class payment solutions to some of the largest banks, traditional financial institutions, and fast-growing fintechs - powered by Wise’s cutting-edge infrastructure.
Wise Platform has already launched transformational partnerships with leading institutions, including significant success across the DACH region with partners like Raiffeisen Bank International, DKB, and N26, alongside other global Tier-1 leaders such as UniCredit, Standard Chartered, and Morgan Stanley.
Switzerland is a core target financial hub for Wise Platform to offer our service. This role provides the opportunity for a senior individual contributor to spearhead and scale this market. Successful candidates can look forward to a career trajectory that supports growth either through a high-impact IC path or into a leadership and management role.
A Bit About the Role
You will sit at the heart of our commercial engine while maintaining the flexibility for a remote structure depending on setup and experience. In this role, you will:
•
Shape the Market Strategy: Act as the strategic bridge between Swiss bank and enterprise clients and our product teams. Your insights into the needs of the local market will directly steer our product roadmap and regional expansion strategy.
•
Unlock Swiss Scale: Take end-to-end responsibility for mapping, pitching, negotiating, and closing partnerships across Tier 1 legacy incumbents, private wealth managers, and challenger banks.
•
Drive Cross-Functional Wins: Collaborate seamlessly with Pre-Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, and Implementation teams to bring highly regulated, complex partnerships to life.
Your Mission
•
Build, maintain, and close a robust pipeline of high-value partnerships across our target verticals in Switzerland Tier 1 banks, regional and private banks, as well as working with fast growth digital challengers and fintechs
•
Create, iterate, and execute our go-to-market strategy, refining localized messaging, commercial pricing strategies, and custom-tailored pitches.
•
Actively manage senior-level stakeholders and navigate complex financial RFP processes within Swiss financial networks.
•
Achieve a realistic but ambitious annual new recurring revenue quota
•
Represent Wise and Wise Platform at industry events and financial conferences across Switzerland.

Qualifications
A Bit About You
•
Language Proficiency: You are fully fluent in German, alongside professional English proficiency.
•
Industry Experience: A minimum of 5 to 8 years of deep experience within payments and/or a specific track record of selling technology products, API infrastructure, or traditional Correspondent Services directly into banks or large financial institutions.
•
Deal Execution: Proven history of managing long, complex enterprise sales cycles from initial top-of-funnel generation down to final legal and economic contract execution.
•
Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with the Swiss banking landscape, including the unique operational structures of cantonal, private, and universal banks, paired with a strong conceptual grasp of how cross-border payment rails operate.
•
Commercial Acumen: Strongly analytical and data-driven; you have a sharp head for economics and are comfortable owning high-value financial negotiations with institutional procurement and C-suite teams.
•
Mindset: An entrepreneurial, hands-on builder who is as excited about mapping out deep technical product integrations with a client as you are closing commercial structures.

Additional Information
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

About This Job
The Role: The Senior Fraud & Financial Crime Analyst – Payments will support the development, optimisation, and ongoing performance management of fraud and financial crime controls for the new Virtual Credit Card (VCC) product. The role is responsible for producing high-quality performance insight, maintaining regulatory and scheme-compliant MI, and driving continuous optimisation of fraud decisioning, rules, and reporting.
This position plays a critical role in ensuring safe VCC launch and stable operational performance post-go-live supporting the Fraud Payments Strategy Manager.
Key Responsibilities:
• Monitor and analyse fraud performance across channels, identifying trends, anomalies, and loss drivers
• Produce and maintain fraud and AML MI, dashboards, and reporting packs for governance and SLT
• Track fraud losses vs plan, supporting root-cause analysis and forecasting
• Analyse AML alerts, typologies, and emerging risks; optimise monitoring rules and reduce false positives
• Ensure sanctions/PEP screening effectiveness and support SAR investigations through transaction analytics
• Own and deliver scheme and regulatory reporting (Visa, Mastercard, PSD2/SCA, FCA) with strong controls
• Conduct transaction-level fraud analysis (e.g. BIN attacks, CNP spikes, merchant risk, wallet performance)
• Develop and refine fraud rules, thresholds, and risk indicators for the VCC ecosystem
• Optimise fraud controls through rule tuning, A/B testing, ML performance improvement, and scenario analysis
• Support UAT, shadow testing, and validation of new fraud solutions ahead of launch
• Maintain and prioritise a backlog of fraud control enhancements with evidence-based recommendations
• Partner cross-functionally (Product, IT, Ops, Compliance, Schemes) to deliver fraud strategy and VCC readiness
• Provide SME input into projects and support customer remediation, disputes, and complaints insight
• Deliver first-line oversight of fraud controls, identifying gaps and driving corrective actions
• Produce incident reporting and post-event analysis for material fraud events
• Maintain robust documentation of processes, analytics, and rule/model changes

Qualifications
• Strong analytical capability using SQL, Python, SAS or similar
• Strong knowledge and experience in card payments data (authorisation, clearing, chargebacks)
• Solid understanding of issuer fraud controls and card scheme reporting (e.g. SAFE, TC40, VFMP, EFM)
• Familiarity with fraud decisioning platforms (e.g. Marqeta, Featurespace, FICO, Ravelin)
• Proven experience in fraud analytics or payments/issuing (typically 3+ years) within an FCA-regulated environment
• Good knowledge of payment types and risks (CNP, CP, tokenised and cross-border flows) and exposure to AML transaction monitoring
• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and identify actionable insights
• Clear communicator, able to translate technical findings for non-technical stakeholders
• High attention to detail, particularly in regulatory and scheme reporting contexts
• Proactive and self-directed, with the ability to take ownership and drive continuous improvement
• Collaborative approach, with experience working cross-functionally across product, operations and risk functions

Additional Information
As FGFS is within a regulated environment any offer is subject to satisfactory background checks including criminal record check, credit check, and employment references.
Along with your benefits package we also offer a wide range of perks for our colleagues:
Frasers Champion - Our employees are at the heart of our business and we ensure individuals are recognised every single month for their hard work. Frasers Champion is a peer nominated scheme where 8 winners will receive double their pay for a month where they have lived the Frasers Group values.
Retail Reconnect – In order to build the planets most admired and compelling brand ecosystem, all employees must understand our business, product and customers. Each financial year, head office employees will gain insights by spending one to two days in one of our stores or the warehouse. The goal is to learn how the work you do impacts our teams on the frontline, and to bring ideas back to the office which will improve how we work.
Fearless 1200 – Fearless 1200 is our way of recognising our growth. It’s bold, ambitious, and designed to reward colleagues across the business for living our values and delivering impact. About This Job
We are looking to work with an experienced self-employed Psychologist (HCPC, UKCP or BPS registered) to practice from our Harley Street rooms.
After room and admin fees, you can expect to earn from £100 per 50-minute session. Administrative support is available six days a week, a dedicated marketing team to promote your services, and our bespoke booking system in place to help you focus on your clinical work.
Given the varied nature of the referrals received, you will be confident in working with a broad range of issues, including complex cases, as long as it is safe to do so in private practice.
Availability requirements
This role prioritises Saturday availability. You will be able to commit to a minimum five-hour clinic on Saturdays, with the option to work longer if desired.
If you wish to offer additional sessions beyond Saturdays, these would take place on weekdays between 4pm and 9pm (with the final client appointment starting at 8pm and finishing at 8.50pm).
Other benefits include:
• no room rental fees when you take time off
• two London-based gatherings each year, offering the chance to meet the wider team in a relaxed setting
• working in sought-after central London locations
• being part of a professional community that values both client care and practitioners’ wellbeing
At Harley Therapy, we place a strong emphasis on long-term professional relationships. We provide robust and responsive administrative support, carefully maintained consulting rooms, and a dedicated marketing team that works continuously to support visibility and appropriate referrals for the practitioners. We also use a bespoke booking and administrative system designed to support efficient repeat appointments and easy access to information around scheduling.
We value continuity highly and place clients at the centre of the work we support. Many of the therapists who work with us have been working with Harley Therapy for over ten years, which we believe is essential in providing consistency, reliability, and a stable therapeutic experience for returning clients. Our ideal candidate would be looking to establish a long-term collaboration, and would prioritise thoughtful and ethical client care.
While practitioners work independently and do not operate as part of a multidisciplinary clinical team, we do place importance on fostering a sense of professional connection. The gatherings organised by Harley Therapy are intended as informal, social opportunities to meet colleagues and the wider team, rather than as clinical or MDT-based forums.
If this approach resonates with you, we would be very pleased to hear from you. You are welcome to include a short note with your application.
Longevity in previous roles and NHS experience is preferred.

Qualifications
Registered with the HCPC, UKCP or BPS.

Additional Information
You will have a minimum of 8 years of experience, preferably more, which includes the years spent seeing clients under supervision during training.

About This Job
The role
This is a senior opportunity to join and lead the London Corporate Transactions & Advisory (CT&A) Product Group's existing Knowledge & Training and Thought Leadership team (K&T and TL team), consisting of experienced Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists.
Our London CT&A Product Group advises on some of the world's largest and most complex M&A transactions, including private M&A, joint ventures, restructurings and corporate advisory work.
Our K&T and TL team is focused on delivering practical and insightful knowhow and advice to lawyers, predominantly in London but also across our global network.  Key to achieving this goal is the need to keep abreast of legal and regulatory developments and work closely with our lawyers in order to ensure that deal and advisory knowhow and insights are collated, analysed and shared across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.
In summary, you will be responsible for ensuring that the London CT&A K&T and TL team delivers on ensuring that lawyers have legal and regulatory knowledge and knowhow at their fingertips, whether that is internal knowhow or knowledge on legal and regulatory developments.
In addition, your particular area of expertise will be company law and corporate governance.  You will keep up to date with, and analyse, all legal and regulatory developments in respect of these areas.  You will also be the "go to" resource for legal and regulatory developments, template maintenance and production, knowledge sharing, training, thought leadership, client communications and AI and innovation in respect of company law and corporate governance.
Your role will also play an important part by ensuring our collective experience is captured and utilised for the benefit of all across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.
You will provide valuable support to the Chair of the CLLS Company Law Committee and any partner on the Company Law Committee of the Law Society, which will involve taking part in working groups, alongside members of these Committees, formed to respond to Government and regulatory body consultations that impact the work of the CT&A Product Group, with a particular focus on company law and corporate governance.
You will also help drive the adoption of legal technology, including the firm's AI tools, by fee earners.  By combining this focus with your legal expertise, you will support the delivery of more efficient, consistent and client-focused legal services.
Who you will work with
You will work in our leading, world-class CT&A Global Product Group, alongside the partners and lawyers.
What makes us one of the most respected Corporate Transactions & Advisory practices globally is our client base, the mandates we win, our industry expertise and commercial approach, and our people and their intellectual capability.  We are consistently retained as lead international counsel on cross-border mandates and our team has a diverse client base that includes a number of FTSE350 and Fortune 500 listed corporations.
You will work within the London CT&A Product Group and also be part of our London and global K&T and TL teams.  This means you will work collaboratively with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in other Product Groups in the London office (including Private Equity, Debt Finance, Employment, Incentives and Real Estate) and in our offices across the globe.
The role more generally and the work supporting the partners involved with the CLLS and Law Society Company Law Committees will provide opportunities to interact with other City law firms, Government departments such as the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) and industry bodies/regulators such as the FCA, the Takeover Panel, Companies House and the FRC.

• Managing the CT&A Knowledge Lawyer team, with responsibility for appraisal reviews, objective setting, performance management and monitoring progress against strategic priorities.

• Preparing and presenting summaries on legal/regulatory developments in respect of company law and corporate governance at London Corporate Knowhow Committee meetings.
Knowledge management and sharing

• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.

• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

About This Job
Building Inspector - Chelsmford
Are you interested in being a Building Inspector? This could be your opportunity to excel as a Building Inspector within one of our Building Control teams, playing a critical role in safeguarding public safety, supporting sustainable building practices, and maintaining high standards in the built environment whilst supporting SOCOTEC’s continued success.
As SOCOTEC grows, so do our teams. We’re looking for a dedicated Building Inspector to join our Building & Real Estate division and wear the SOCOTEC badge with pride.
We are seeking a proactive, reliable, and flexible Building Inspector to join the Building Control team. In this role, you will be inspecting construction sites at various stages, advising on regulatory requirements, and working collaboratively with architects, builders and developers to ensure safe, structurally sound, and code-compliant buildings.
The tasks you will undertake will include (but are not limited to):
• Conduct comprehensive site inspections and regulatory assessments – Perform building inspections at various construction stages to ensure compliance with Building Regulations, review structural, architectural, and mechanical designs, assess building materials, construction specifications, and fire strategies against relevant Building Regulations and allied legislation
• Supervise inspection activities and enforce regulatory compliance – Act as a Registered Building Inspector within your competency and registered class, supervise lower-class RBIs and graduate trainees, interpret and enforce national and local building regulations (including fire safety, energy efficiency, accessibility, and environmental requirements), and issue formal notices on compliance breaches under the Building Safety Act 2022
• Prepare detailed compliance documentation and provide consultancy services – Produce comprehensive inspection reports, compliance certificates, and regulatory approval documentation, maintain accurate records ensuring traceability and compliance with local authority requirements, and assist clients with Building Regulations consultancy advice where SOCOTEC is not acting as the Registered Building Control Approver

Qualifications
To be a successful  Building Inspector, you should be able to demonstrate:
• Professional qualification and regulatory registration at senior level – Hold membership of RICS, CABE or equivalent (or be qualified by suitable experience), ensure CPD requirements are met to broaden and develop skills, and demonstrate compliance through registration as an RBI at an appropriate level
• Excellent communication and client relationship management skills – Demonstrate strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities to work effectively with clients and deliver excellent client care across all interactions and project engagements
• Self-starting problem-solver with technical expertise – Show ability to work independently as well as part of large project teams, analyse complex issues, develop suitable solutions, implement these solutions effectively, and keep up to date with changes in building codes, regulations, and industry best practices

Additional Information
Why SOCOTEC?
Join a thriving community of over 2,000 industry professionals who are passionate about making a real difference. At SOCOTEC UK, we're not just delivering services - we're shaping the future of testing, inspection, and certification across the nation.
What sets us apart? Our people. We've built our reputation on attracting exceptional talent like you and empowering them to deliver excellence at every turn. Our comprehensive range of TIC services means you'll have the opportunity to work on diverse, challenging projects that truly matter.
In this role, you won't just be another employee - you'll be a key player in our continued success story. Your expertise will directly contribute to our mission of building a safer, more sustainable world, while you grow your career alongside some of the industry's finest professionals.
Your Career, Your Way
Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.
Work Your Way
Local, national, or global projects. Office-based, remote, or hybrid. We offer the flexibility that empowers you to perform at your best.
Committed to Your Growth
From day one, you'll have access to comprehensive training, mentorship, and development programs. We support every step of your professional journey. #YouGrowWeGrow
Think you've got what it takes to add value to our success? We would love to hear from you and look forward to receiving your application.

We are looking for an experienced Change Manager with a strong background in contractual change, project controls and commercial project delivery to join our team.
This is a project-focused change management role, responsible for managing contractual and commercial changes throughout the project lifecycle. The successful candidate will work closely with Project Management, Commercial, Planning, Cost and Contract teams to ensure changes are properly identified, assessed, documented, approved and incorporated into the project baseline.
The role will be critical in ensuring that changes to scope, cost, programme, deliverables and contractual obligations are clearly understood and effectively controlled.
Key Responsibilities
•
Manage the end-to-end contractual change control process across projects and programmes.
•
Identify, record and assess changes arising from scope, design development, client instructions, contractor proposals, unforeseen circumstances and other project events.
•
Ensure all changes are formally documented, tracked and progressed through the appropriate approval process.
•
Work closely with Commercial and Contract Management teams to assess the contractual and commercial implications of proposed changes.
•
Coordinate with Planning and Project Controls teams to assess the programme and schedule impact of changes.
•
Work with Cost teams to understand and validate the cost impact of changes.
•
Ensure changes are appropriately reflected in project baselines, forecasts and reporting.
•
Maintain accurate and up-to-date change registers and supporting documentation.
•
Track changes from initial identification through assessment, approval, implementation and close-out.
•
Prepare change papers, reports and recommendations for project and governance review.
•
Monitor outstanding changes and ensure actions and approvals are progressed within agreed timescales.
•
Review change submissions and supporting information to ensure they are complete, accurate and properly substantiated.
•
Identify potential changes and ensure they are captured early to minimise impact on project delivery.
•
Support the assessment of contractor and supplier change requests, variations and compensation events.
•
Ensure contractual notices and change documentation are aligned with relevant contract requirements.
•
Provide regular reporting on change status, value, programme impact, trends and emerging issues.
•
Analyse change trends to identify recurring issues, scope gaps, design development or other drivers of project change.
•
Support project teams in maintaining a clear audit trail of all approved and rejected changes.
•
Contribute to continuous improvement of project change control processes, procedures and governance.
About You
We are looking for a commercially aware and detail-focused Change Manager who understands how contractual change can affect the cost, programme, scope and overall delivery of a project.
You will ideally have:
•
Proven experience in contractual change management, project controls, commercial management or contract administration.
•
Experience working on complex projects or programmes within energy, infrastructure, construction, engineering or other major capital projects.
•
Strong understanding of the relationship between scope, cost, programme and contractual change.
•
Experience managing change registers and formal change control processes.
•
Good understanding of contract mechanisms relating to variations, change orders, compensation events, instructions and claims.
•
Experience assessing the impact of change on project cost and schedule.
•
Strong understanding of project controls and how changes affect the approved project baseline.
•
Experience working closely with Commercial, Planning, Cost, Project Management and Contract teams.
•
Strong analytical and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail.
•
Ability to interpret contractual and project documentation and identify potential change.
•
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
•
Confidence challenging information and ensuring changes are properly substantiated.
•
Ability to manage multiple changes across a complex project environment.

About This Job
As Senior Risk Analyst, you will be an integral part of project delivery which is designed to positively contribute, influence and underpin success across Engineering, Procurement & Manufacturing, Construction & Commissioning of a Nuclear Power Station project. The Risk team is aligned to the three critical success factors to successfully deliver the project objectives and underpin stakeholder confidence i.e. Integrated baseline delivery; EPC critical path execution; and key milestone achievement to Commercial Operation Date (COD).
Further to this the programme is influenced by the following:
• The Nuclear environment – this is highly regulated by the Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR) and the job holder will be responsible for supporting delivery in the nuclear context
• Nuclear Safety Culture – this is of paramount importance to the Project and embedded throughout for which the job holder will be responsible for supporting delivery with this in mind.
• Recognising the importance of the delivery of the project in accordance with the principles of safety, quality, time and cost in that order of priority.
In order to work in this operating environment, the jobholder will be familiar with the following key documents and support others in understanding:
• Company Manual – outlines the purpose of the company
• Project Execution & Business Plan – describes the delivery strategy for the Project
• Project Delivery Model – signposts readers to key procedures
• Integrated Project Controls Manual – how work is undertaken in the Project Controls Function
• Discipline-specific Procedures – detailed activity steps, interfaces, etc.
Responsibilities:
• The Senior Risk Analyst will be the face of Risk management in their nominated Programme/Area in the Project, bringing confidence to stakeholders that they are performing the right steps to identify, analyse, respond to and manage their Risk Outputs.
• Providing assurance of the maintenance of all Risk and Opportunity data for the Programme/Area within the Risk software system e.g. ARM.
• Assurance of the delivery of Risk and Opportunity reports to a defined reporting cycle, including commentary on key time-related drivers and performance issues ensuring the quality of the output
• Reviewing and challenging the significant issues that may impact programme/area objective
• Supporting issue and opportunities reviews and workshops and specialist risk focussed sessions (i.e. scenario planning).
• Analysis of risk data and the connection of this data across the Project, in conjunction with the project controls managers and risk leads;
• Challenging the uncertainties of risk data over time to allow prioritisation and decision making.
• Ensuring a comprehensive risk portfolio is maintained and reflective of the current project position.
• Working with colleagues in IPC to ensure that the Project schedule and cost estimates are informed by high quality risk information (at delivery and portfolio levels).
• Work with the PCM's to support the programme/area teams and where appropriate Tier 1 Contractors to assess contractor-held Risk and their views on Programme-held risks and opportunities that impact upon them.
• Identify and support the implementation of enhancements to integrated risk management procedure, process, reporting and tools.
• Accountable for the production and presentation of accurate, insightful project controls information at the Programme Reviews and Board Meetings, ROTCs, Portfolio Risk Review as required.
• Responsible for the management and verification of information within the PowerBI dashboards and providing proposals for improvement from the Programme/Area teams.
• Lead Risk management and Risk software specific training to the Programme/Area team, PM community and apprentices and provide recommendations of additional training requirements, or improvements to existing training.

Qualifications
Qualifications & Experience
• Desirable degree level or equivalent qualification in project management, project controls, engineering, or another related field
• Industry recognised project controls and/or risk management qualifications, such as Management of Risk Practitioner and/or APM Risk Level 2.
• Demonstrable experience of working as an expert in risk management and expert knowledge of risk/project controls including the tools, and a variety of techniques used to deliver project insight and assess performance
• Experience of working in a project management environment and desirable construction experience
• Experience of working in the Nuclear Industry or other highly regulated industry
Knowledge & Skills
• Able to deliver accurate and concise Risk insights to drive evidence-based decision making, utilising commercial and technical information, to influence project decisions and support the management of risks/opportunities.
• Understanding and/or practical experience of wider project controls disciplines enabling Risk management to be integrated with cost, schedule and change, and provide assurance that risk and opportunity reporting and outputs of risk analysis aligns with other project data.
• Excellent analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
• Proven ability to facilitate risk conversations with colleagues at all levels, including Executive and Director leadership.
• Effectively communicates complex issues and concepts (unique insights) in simple ways, to both technical and non-technical senior audiences.
• Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and delegate tasks to other team members.
• Possesses high work standards and sets ambitious, yet attainable goals. Constantly drives to streamline and simplify to deliver business value.
• Ability to effectively collaborate with colleagues within and across organisational boundaries to achieve mutually successful outcomes.
• Ability to assure the quality of others work supporting them in developing to effectively deliver outputs.
• Ability to expertly use and guide others in the use of Risk management software;
• Ability to draw from best practice across industry to implement changes for improved performance.
Tools and Software

• Managing your productions through to delivery, proactively communicating any changes or issues that could affect schedules.

• Previous experience gained in audio production, whether that be in audiobooks, radio or podcasts, including experience working in a studio environment.
• An understanding of audio technology, including recording interfaces, recording software, microphones, and compressors.
• Experience directing actors and readers for the best possible audio performance.
• Creativity and fresh ideas about how to produce innovative, market-leading audiobooks.
• Confidence working with senior stakeholders across a range of projects.

About This Job
Building Inspector - Chichester
Are you interested in being a Building Inspector? This could be your opportunity to excel as a Building Inspector within one of our Building Control teams, playing a critical role in safeguarding public safety, supporting sustainable building practices, and maintaining high standards in the built environment whilst supporting SOCOTEC’s continued success.
As SOCOTEC grows, so do our teams. We’re looking for a dedicated Building Inspector to join our Building & Real Estate division and wear the SOCOTEC badge with pride.
We are seeking a proactive, reliable, and flexible Building Inspector to join the Building Control team. In this role, you will be inspecting construction sites at various stages, advising on regulatory requirements, and working collaboratively with architects, builders and developers to ensure safe, structurally sound, and code-compliant buildings.
The tasks you will undertake will include (but are not limited to):
• Conduct comprehensive site inspections and regulatory assessments – Perform building inspections at various construction stages to ensure compliance with Building Regulations, review structural, architectural, and mechanical designs, assess building materials, construction specifications, and fire strategies against relevant Building Regulations and allied legislation
• Supervise inspection activities and enforce regulatory compliance – Act as a Registered Building Inspector within your competency and registered class, supervise lower-class RBIs and graduate trainees, interpret and enforce national and local building regulations (including fire safety, energy efficiency, accessibility, and environmental requirements), and issue formal notices on compliance breaches under the Building Safety Act 2022
• Prepare detailed compliance documentation and provide consultancy services – Produce comprehensive inspection reports, compliance certificates, and regulatory approval documentation, maintain accurate records ensuring traceability and compliance with local authority requirements, and assist clients with Building Regulations consultancy advice where SOCOTEC is not acting as the Registered Building Control Approver

Qualifications
To be a successful  Building Inspector, you should be able to demonstrate:
• Professional qualification and regulatory registration at senior level – Hold membership of RICS, CABE or equivalent (or be qualified by suitable experience), ensure CPD requirements are met to broaden and develop skills, and demonstrate compliance through registration as an RBI at an appropriate level
• Excellent communication and client relationship management skills – Demonstrate strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities to work effectively with clients and deliver excellent client care across all interactions and project engagements
• Self-starting problem-solver with technical expertise – Show ability to work independently as well as part of large project teams, analyse complex issues, develop suitable solutions, implement these solutions effectively, and keep up to date with changes in building codes, regulations, and industry best practices

Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.
Work Your Way

Committed to Your Growth
From day one, you'll have access to comprehensive training, mentorship, and development programs. We support every step of your professional journey. #YouGrowWeGrow

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001442.description_excerpt:
About This Job
IFS builds enterprise software for the industries that run the world – energy, manufacturing, construction, aerospace and telecom among them. As AI moves from pilot to daily practice across our Product Management organization, we need someone who can turn that shift into practical , adopted ways of working that help teams make better decisions and reduce friction at scale.
We're looking for someone who can bring structure to complex, cross-functional problems – identifying root causes, creating practical solutions, and helping teams adopt better ways of working at scale.
This role sits at the intersection of portfolio management, product management and financial/commercial planning, with AI-agentic first ways of working central to the role.  You will use AI tools as your default way of working, and  prototype  and implement reusable agents, data products and automated workflows that remove friction at scale.
You'll report into IFS Product & Technology Strategy & Planning organization, working closely with Product Management leadership. This is an individual-contributor role. Your impact is measured in influence, clarity and adopted capabilities.
You can be located in any of these countries; UK, Netherlands, Poland, Sweden or Sri Lanka
•
Portfolio insight and decision enablement – turn portfolio data, initiative context and business signals into self-serve insights, decision tools and clear options that help product managers and leaders make better-informed prioritization, investment and sequencing decisions.
•
Predictive and scenario-based portfolio analysis – go beyond reporting on the past: build predictive models that forecast portfolio outcomes, and model alternative scenarios, trade-offs and opportunity costs – a capability we don't have today – so leadership can compare real options instead of relying on gut feel.
•
Capital allocation and ROI – develop clear, evidence-based recommendations for how investment should be allocated across products and define how ROI and benefits realization are tracked once decisions are made.
•
Strategy support – use AI-powered knowledge management to make our strategy and roadmap easier to consume and act on and use portfolio insight to pressure-test it – are we funding the strategy we set out to fund, are we spread too thin, are we over-investing in areas with limited growth potential.
•
Root cause analysis – dig past symptoms to understand why the same friction keeps recurring across teams and help design sustainable solutions rather than local workarounds.
•
Turning ambiguity into scalable capability – clarify ambiguous requirements, translate recurring organizational friction into repeatable processes, operating models and and help teams adopt AI-enabled solutions broadly rather than solved repeatedly as one-off problems.
•
Agentic enablement – design, prototype and deploy AI agents, workflows and decision-support tools that scale across the product management organization, replacing repetitive analysis and coordination work with reusable capabilities.
•
Enablement over control – create the tools, data products, AI agents and operating mechanisms that allow product managers to work more independently and effectively, reducing reliance on central coordination while increasing consistency and decision quality.

Qualifications
You do not need to meet every point below. We are most interested in candidates who can combine strong portfolio/product thinking with analytical judgement, curiosity about AI-enabled ways of working, and the ability to translate complexity into practical, adopted solutions.
Essential experience and capabilities
•
Background in product operations, portfolio management, product management, or a closely related role, with solid grounding in product planning, roadmapping, prioritisation or portfolio governance.
•
Financial and commercial fluency – comfortable modelling portfolio scenarios, trade-offs and opportunity costs, and framing recommendations in terms of ROI and benefits realisation that leadership can act on.
•
Comfort operating at the portfolio level – able to turn complex prioritisation and sequencing questions into clear data, evidence and options, so Product Managers and leaders can make confident, well-informed decisions across multiple teams and initiatives.
•
Practical confidence using modern AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot to improve analysis, decision-making or ways of working.
•
A strong preference for enabling teams through better tools, clearer processes, self-serve answers and AI-enabled ways of working, rather than centralising decisions or becoming a gatekeeper.
•
Comfort clarifying ambiguous requirements, shaping a path forward and working with stakeholders to build alignment.
Desirable experience
•
Hands-on experience building or configuring AI agents, workflows or self-service tools, for example via Claude, MCP-style tool integrations, Copilot or low-code agent platforms.
•
Enough understanding of how software gets built in an AI-assisted world to partner credibly with engineering; you do not need to ship production code, but you understand how the work has changed.
•
Experience in enterprise software or B2B SaaS product organisations.
•
Familiarity with portfolio management frameworks.
•
Exposure to data governance, anonymisation, or data-sharing agreements.

Additional Information
We believe that coming together as a community, in person, is important for innovation, connection and fostering a sense of belonging. Our roles have the right balance of remote and in-office working to enable flexibility for managing your life along with ensuring a real connection with your colleagues and the broader IFS community.

As the Director, UKI CRM Solution Consulting, you run the day-to-day pre-sales engine for CRM across the UK, Ireland, and Scotland. You lead first-line Solution Consulting managers and their individual contributors, and you are the leader closest to the deals.
You know what each team is working on, what is landing with customers, and what is stalling. Your job is to remove the blockers, keep the team focused and motivated, and make sure Solution Consulting moves in step with its CRM selling peers. You report to the AVP, EMEA CRM Solution Consulting, who sets regional strategy and direction.

Own the number -- deliver CRM NNACV for UKI
• Carry accountability, with your first-line managers, for UKI CRM NNACV targets and contribute to the EMEA goal of double-digit ACV growth.
• Forecast technical win rates and deal-by-deal readiness, and raise risk to the AVP early rather than late.
• Work with UKI CRM sales leaders to focus Solution Consulting time on the opportunities, use cases, and industries where CRM wins fastest.
Know the deals on the ground
• Maintain a detailed, current view of what each team is working on: active opportunities, technical stage, proof-of-value status, and next steps.
• Know what is working and what is not, and act on it in the weekly deal and pipeline rhythms rather than in a quarterly review.
• Join key customer, POV, and escalation discussions where technical credibility or senior air cover is needed.
Remove blockers and keep the team focused
• Be the first escalation point for anything that slows a deal: environment access, resourcing conflicts, unclear scope, product gaps, or competing demands.
• Protect the team's time by clearing distractions, cutting low-value requests, and making sure ICs spend their time on the deals that matter most.
• Make sure every IC knows what good looks like on their deals and has what they need to deliver it.
Lead and develop first-line leaders and ICs
• Coach first-line managers on deal reviews, technical strategy, and POV execution, and hold them to consistent motions and communication rhythms.
• Recruit, develop, and retain strong technical talent, and build a bench of ready-now first-line leaders.
• Give direct, regular feedback to ICs and managers, and address performance issues early.
Keep the team motivated and aligned to selling peers
• Recognize wins visibly and often, and build a team rhythm that keeps morale and momentum high.
• Run joint pipeline and deal reviews with CRM sales, value, partner, and product counterparts so Solution Consulting and selling teams operate as one engine.
• Agree coverage, account plans, and proof strategy with the AEs before they reach the customer.
Drive the shift to POV-centric selling and the FDE model
• Make working proof-of-value the default way the team earns technical trust, and help ICs move toward the Forward Deployed Engineer model of building alongside customers.
• Use AI automation tools and standard POV frameworks to speed up demos, environment provisioning, and repeatable assets.
Connect the field to CRM product
• Channel technical wins, losses, and product gaps from your team to the AVP and CRM product leaders, using specific, deal-level examples.

Qualifications

• 6+ years in a leadership role in Solution Consulting or a comparable pre-sales or technical sales function, including managing first-line leaders and individual contributors.

• A consistent record of owning and delivering against ACV / NNACV or equivalent revenue-tied targets in a software or SaaS environment.
• Experience leading distributed teams across the UK, Ireland, and Scotland and operating effectively across cultures, languages, and time zones.
• A working understanding of the CRM market and how AI and agentic automation are changing it.
• Fluency with AI and automation tools and a bias toward using them to simplify how work gets done.

• Clear, direct communication, and the ability to set a standard and hold first-line leaders to it.
• Good operating judgement: knows when to escalate, when to decide, and when to get out of the way.

About This Job
The salary for this role is £57,117 (inclusive of a Specialist Allowance).
This role can be based at any of the following sites: Culham, Oxfordshire.
Please be aware that this role is subject to achieving a UK Security Vetting (UKSV) including The Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS) checks for criminal convictions and possibly a search of open source data. For this role the UKSV level is Security Clearance (SC). You must either hold SC clearance with no restrictions or be able to achieve it. Note: the UK residency criteria for SC is a minimum of 2 out of the last 5 years, at least one year of which must be 12 consecutive months. For further information please refer to The UKAEA recruitment process | UKAEA Careers.
UKAEA is an onsite organisation, and this role requires regular onsite presence (usually between 3-5 days in any given week) in line with business needs. We actively support flexible working arrangements where this is compatible with the role.
The Role
The fusion industry is growing in the UK and internationally, with the initiation of long-term projects to design and build future fusion power plant on the path to commercialisation of fusion power.  This includes UKAEA’s STEP prototype reactor, in support of UKAEA Goals, to solve challenges of sustainable fusion energy.
To support these advances, the future safety, security and environmental regulatory framework for fusion power plant must be developed, to ensure that it is proportionate to the hazard profile of fusion, and enabling of the innovative approaches to fusion plant design.
The Fusion Safety Advisory (FSA) team plays a key role in the development of UK’s international regulatory framework for fusion power, and also internationally. To achieve this, the team provides technical fusion safety advice, guidance and technical support to DESNZ, Regulatory Bodies and international groups, such as the IAEA.  The team also engages with domestic and international fusion groups and companies in areas of fusion safety, security and environment.
Nationally, this will include working with and advising government, as well as assisting regulatory bodies, contributing to pivotal strategic industry documents and technical fusion safety guidance.  Internationally, the UK has built a leading reputation in the development of proportionate fusion regulation, and the job holder will help to preserve this reputation and influence the world stage by collaborating closely with international groups, such as IAEA and others. The job holder will build and maintain relations with organisations across the fusion sector, supporting working groups as required on focal regulatory topics, as such travel will be required.
Key Responsibilities:
• Taking main responsibility for high-level radiological consequence assessment for postulated accident scenarios and using this underpinning technical work to guide the development of fusion safety, security and environmental regulation both domestically and internationally. This may be as a direct contributor or as intelligent customer, as required. Note that due to the First of a Kind nature of fusion developments, these high-level radiological consequence assessments are undertaken with emerging conceptual design information in order to inform a developing sector
• Providing specialist fusion safety, security and environment input into strategic and technical documentation supporting the development of the national and international regulatory framework for the future fusion industry
• Planning regulatory familiarisation and training in fusion by providing site visits and subject matter expert presentations
• Proactive interaction with other fusion organisations and regulatory bodies, both in the UK and internationally, to support the harmonisation of fusion safety regulation
• Actively participating as UK representative in national and international fusion industry workshops to develop standards and guidance in safety, security, environmental protection and waste management
• Providing technical review, advice and guidance in response to questions relating to fusion safety regulation in alignment with the UK’s fusion strategy.

Qualifications
Essential Requirements:
• A degree in an engineering or scientific discipline enhanced by experience or post-graduate qualification; or equivalent combination of relevant qualifications and/or experience
• Working knowledge of regulations and guidance in safety, security, environmental protection and waste management
• Experience in radiological consequence assessment, identifying hazards, release mechanisms and possible sequence of events that could develop under postulated accident scenarios
• Experience of modelling releases to various pathways and receptors on and off-site, for conceptual fusion power plant designs, using software, such as ADMS and PACE
• Demonstrable knowledge of how to apply theoretical, high-level radiological consequence assessment to wider risk and policy considerations, such as emergency preparedness and insurance & third party liability, with clear risk messaging for relevant stakeholders
• Confident ownership of tasks and the ability to work to deadlines.

Additional Information
A full list of our benefits can be found here https://careers.ukaea.uk/life-at-ukaea/employee-benefits/
UKAEA’s mission is clean energy for all, and we welcome talented people from all backgrounds to help us achieve this goal. We are committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion and strive to ensure fair representation across our workforce. We particularly encourage applications from groups currently underrepresented in STEM, including women and individuals from diverse ethnic backgrounds, while ensuring all appointments are made on merit.
UK Atomic Energy Authority is committed to being accessible. Please email talent@ukaea.uk if you have any questions or require help or adjustments to compete on a fair basis, for example, changes to the way we interview or share information.
Please note that vacancies are generally advertised for 4 weeks but may close earlier if we receive a large number of applications.

Owning design problems in your team and working through the detail to create solutions that balance the need to design ahead with delivering incremental value.

Shaping the now, next and future state of the experience, and holding the work to the outcomes we've committed to.

Bringing systems thinking to your work and collaborating with other teams to ensure we create one coherent experience.

Building vision with substance through evidence backed direction that shapes the roadmap.

Using AI in your daily practice where it earns its place, and showing the team what that looks like.

Be part of a positive change in the world. We're fixing a broken, greedy system, and giving businesses control of their money.

You've been the most senior designer on a complex product area, owning ambiguous problems end to end. The title matters less than the scope.
